Drama at Armonia is part of one package: music, drama and dance performance, together. Children work with voice, character and movement, and along the way they grow in confidence and learn to carry a piece as a team. What a session feels like A rehearsal room, not a classroom. Sessions run in small groups, and the same group returns week after week, so a scene has time to grow. Children try a moment one way and then another: how a line sounds, how a character stands, how a movement lands. Getting it wrong in front of friends is part of the work, and that is where the confidence comes from. What a performance feels like The performances children work toward are ELC occasions, with the whole school behind them. At a drama night nobody auditions for a place: every child takes a part, and every child gets a moment at the centre of the stage. In expressive languages, children explore their ideas through drawing, painting and building, treating each material as another language for thinking. They work with real materials and real tools, and a piece can carry over many sessions until it says what they mean. What a session feels like A studio, not an art lesson. Children choose a material and get to work: clay, wire, paint, light, paper, found objects. The adult watches closely and asks the next question rather than showing the answer. Children work in small groups and return to their work week after week, so a drawing or a build has time to grow until it carries the meaning they intend. Music at Armonia is part of one package: music, drama and dance performance, together. Making music feeds nearly every part of how a child grows: thinking, feeling, movement and language, and with them the quieter habits of self-discipline and confidence. What a session feels like Small groups, real instruments. Children play alone and together, from a single line to a full ensemble, and both matter: musicianship stretches how a young brain organises itself and grows. The same group returns week after week, so a piece has time to get good before anyone else hears it. What a performance feels like A concert is a child's way of showing their family what they have been learning, and at ELC the whole community turns up to listen. When the school stages a musical, whole year groups share the stage: Wonderland the Musical packed the courtyard at night, with every child making a role their own. Read the story on our blog. ELC Portal v0.7 This week Activities Calendar Purple Elephant PE 39, 49 & 55 PE Samakee Policies FAQ Quick answers New families Glossary Nuts and bolts This week / Activities / Armonia / Science Armonia · Science Real questions, tested. Science here is hands-on investigation. Children start from their own questions, test their thinking with real materials, and follow the evidence wherever it leads. What a session feels like A workshop, not a worksheet. Science sessions start from children's own questions, and children test their thinking with real materials and careful observation. They practise the habits scientists actually use: noticing closely, predicting, checking and trying again. That is how children already work across ELC. One Year 4 class designed a planet of its own, debating its size, core and terrain as a group, then put its questions directly to a NASA scientist, whose advice was to stay curious and keep asking. The same habits carry into the garden, where children watch what grows and work out why. Technology here means making, code and robotics as tools for ideas. Children move from using technology to building with it, designing things that respond to what they imagine. What a session feels like Build, test, build again. In technology sessions children move from using technology to making with it, designing and building things that respond to their ideas. Children at ELC already work this way. A Year 3 class sketched robot designs in their notebooks, then worked together to code a real robot's movements, and children in the rewilding project designed and built machines that answered real needs they had noticed in the school garden. It rarely works the first time, and that is the point: children read what went wrong, change one thing and build again. b: ELC Portal v0.7 This week Activities Calendar Purple Elephant PE 39, 49 & 55 PE Samakee Policies FAQ Quick answers New families Glossary Nuts and bolts This week / Privacy Privacy What this site knows about you: nothing. No login. No accounts. No cookies. No trackers. No child data. This page explains what that means, and where your information does live when you sign up for something. A promise you can check This site is a set of plain pages. It sets no cookies, keeps no accounts, loads no advertising scripts, and serves everything, including its fonts, from its own address. We count which pages get opened so we know what helps; the counter stores the page address, including any campaign tag on a link we sent, and nothing else; there is no cookie, no fingerprint, and nothing that identifies you, and you can verify this in your browser's developer tools. If you install this site as an app, the pages are stored on your own device so they open offline. Only that page-open count is ever sent back to us.
